Learned advocate Ms.Shivangi Rana waives service of notice of Rule for respondent No.2 and learned APP Mr.Soham Joshi waives service of notice of Rule for the respondents State.
2.

Considering the issue involved in the present application and with consent of the learned advocates appearing for the respective parties as well as considering the fact that the dispute amongst the petitioner and respondent - original complainant has been resolved amicably, this matter is taken up for final disposal forthwith.

3. sentences.text: 5. Seeking quashment of the FIR qua the petitioner, learned advocate Mr.Timbalia submits that the role of the present petitioner is limited to giving slap to the complainant/prosecutrix and speaking filthy and derogatory language.
Apart from that, there is no other allegation levelled against the present petitioner.
He would further submit that the present petitioner is sister of the main accused.
He would further submit that prosecutrix has entered into compromise with the main accused and she is expected to depose before the learned Sessions Court.
Upon above submissions, learned advocate Mr.Timbalia submits to quash the questioned FIR.
6. Learned advocate Ms.Shivangi Rana appearing for respondent No.2 - prosecutrix having tendered the affidavit on behalf of the complainant submits that she has identified the prosecutrix.
She has also explained the contents of the affidavit and interpreted the same in local language to the prosecutrix.
She would further submit that the prosecutrix without any pressure or coercion has entered into compromise with the main accused as well.
Therefore, she submits that prosecutrix has no objection to quash the questioned FIR.
The affidavit of the prosecutrix is taken on record.
7. The prosecutrix herself has remained present in the Court.
She being a major lady submitted to the Court that she has NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/1805/2018 ORDER DATED: 09/04/2025 undefined understood what is stated in the affidavit.
She has been interpreted and explained the contents of the affidavit.
She submits that she has entered into compromise with the main accused without any coercion or threat.
She submits that she has no objection if the FIR in question is quashed.

8. Considering the role played by the petitioner and further considering the statement of the prosecutrix on oath filed before the Court by way of affidavit, in which she has stated as under :
"2. I state that after filing of the aforesaid FIR, an amicable settlement has arrived at between me and applicant and I have decided to enter into compromise by sorting out our differences and we have amicably resolved our disputes.
I have no grievance against the applicant and I have no objection if the impugned FIR and consequential proceedings arising thereto are quashed.
3. I state that FIR was a result of misunderstanding and the name of the applicant was mentioned due to some misunderstanding which is now cleared.
Thus, I have no objection if the same is quashed.
I state that I have no grievance against the applicant and I have no objection if the aforesaid FIR and all other consequential proceedings thereto are quashed."

Having heard the learned counsel for the respective parties, considering the facts and circumstances arising out of the present application as well as taking into consideration the decisions rendered in the cases of Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab & Anr., reported in (2012) 10 SCC 303, Madan Mohan NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/1805/2018 ORDER DATED: 09/04/2025 undefined Abbot Vs. State of Punjab, reported in (2008) 4 SCC 582, Nikhil Merchant Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation & Anr., reported in 2009 (1) GLH 31, Manoj Sharma Vs. State & Ors.,
reported in 2009 (1) GLH 190 and Narinder Singh & Ors. Vs. State of Punjab & Anr. reported in 2014 (2) Crime 67 (SC) as well as State of Haryana Vs. Bhajanlal reported in AIR 1992 SC 604, it appears that further continuation of criminal proceedings in relation to the impugned FIR against the petitioner would be unnecessary harassment to the applicant.
